Issued at 300 PM EDT Thu Oct 29 2026

Rest of Today-Friday...The mid-upper level pattern begins to 
amplify, driven by deepening troughs over the Pacific coast, and 
in the western North Atlantic. Ridging builds over the central to 
eastern US in response, though a lobe of vorticity caught in the 
pattern will cause some disruption of the ridge structure as it 
lifts from Mexico and Texas into the Central Plains, before 
elongating across much of the eastern US. The building ridge 
ushers weak low pressure near the Bahamas out sea, and along with 
surface high pressure diving southeast from the northern 
US/Canada, reinforces surface high pressure over the eastern US. 
The southern flank of the strengthening high settles over Central
Florida, keeping the pressure gradient relatively tight while
gradually veering flow from northeasterly to more easterly. 
Gusty/breezy conditions are forecast in the afternoons (gusts 
20-25 mph, possibly up to 30 mph at times), with gentler winds 
overnight. While winds and King Tides are slowly relenting, and 
the highest water levels are in the rear-view mirror, we won't 
shake the coastal flooding until the weekend, and dangerous beach 
conditions are likely to persist through the weekend. The Coastal
Flood Warning has been allowed to expire, but a Coastal Flood 
Advisory takes its place through Friday for minor coastal flood 
and beach erosion during the high tides, especially the higher 
tide Friday in the late morning/early afternoon. A High Surf 
Advisory remains in effect today for breaking waves up to 7 ft, 
and while wave heights are forecast to drop below criteria 
Friday, the surf will remain rough and continue to produce life- 
threatening rip currents. A Rip Current Statement remains in 
effect.

Drier air filtering towards Florida around the high will still 
have higher than normal moisture, knocking rain chances down but 
not eliminating them. Isolated to scattered showers currently 
moving onshore (which are expected to continue the next several
days) are much spottier than previous days, greatly reducing the 
heavy rainfall threat. That said, decreased cloud cover has 
opened the door for more effective destabilization from daytime 
heating, and this morning's soundings lack the inversions that 
were capping updraft growth for many days (despite model soundings
still sporting them), providing a more favorable environment for 
deep convection. Overall instability will be limited by very warm
mid-levels and frankly pathetic lapse rates. All together, can't 
rule out isolated lightning storms capable of occasional cloud to 
ground lightning. Gusts to around 45 mph due to drier air aloft,
and brief downpours will be possible with any storms and heavy 
showers that manage to form. Highest chances for lightning storms,
such as they are at 20% or less, will be in the afternoons and 
evenings, but isolated onshore moving heavy showers will be 
possible around the clock. Temperatures seasonally warm with highs
in the L-M80s and lows in the U60s-M70s. 

Halloween...Not quite the trick-or-treating weather we'd hope 
for, as onshore flow keeps rain chances above normal in gusty and 
humid conditions. Central Florida remains under the southern flank
of deep high pressure over the eastern US sliding towards the 
coast. The relatively tight pressure gradient will produce 
breezy/gusty onshore (easterly) flow in the afternoon and evening,
with gusts 25-30 mph. While still drier than earlier this week, 
above normal moisture will keep the humidity higher than we'd 
like, and support isolated to scattered showers in the afternoon, 
evening, and overnight. There is a low risk (20% chance or less) 
for isolated lightning storms capable of occasional cloud to 
ground lightning. Storms that manage to form and heavy showers 
will also be capable of brief downpours, and drier air aloft could
help produce wind gusts to around 45 mph. Temperatures remain 
seasonably warm with highs in the L-M80s and lows in the L-M70s, 
with trick-or-treating temperatures in the U-M70s, up to around 80
along the southernmost coast.

At the beaches, surf will remain rough and dangerous with 
numerous life-threatening rip currents present. Entering the water
is not advised. In the Atlantic waters, poor to hazardous boating
conditions will linger, especially in the Gulf Stream. 

Sunday-Wednesday (Modified Previous Discussion)...The setup 
appears favorable for an uptick in rain and even isolated (20%) 
lightning coverage, and statistical guidance keeps rain chances to
60-80% on Sunday. The deep onshore flow combined with modest 
upper jet diffluence is at least somewhat concerning for the 
potential of locally heavy rain. This may lead to flooding of 
poorly drained areas, especially along the coast on Sunday.
